source.title: Deep learning generalizes because the parameter-function map is biased towards simple functions
source.authors: Guillermo Valle Pérez; Chico Q. Camargo; A. Louis

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present and readable. Some typographical and PDF extraction errors appear, but they do not prevent extraction of the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains neural networks with gradient-based methods and reports training error, directly measuring whether training reaches zero error in the tested settings.
record.gate_note: Section 6 states training set error was 0 in all experiments. The paper also reports that plain SGD often failed to reach zero error on the Boolean-function task, while advSGD succeeded in almost all cases. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports zero training classification error for its CNN on binarized CIFAR-10 across tested label-corruption conditions. This bears on V1 in a changed task setting, although the paper primarily studies generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the main argument: an intrinsic bias toward simple functions helps explain generalization, supported by function-sampling experiments and PAC-Bayes bounds. The authors treat SGD's approximation to Bayesian sampling as provisional. Zero benchmark training error and Boolean-task SGD failures are experimental observations; the latter appears in Appendix A and a Section 7 footnote, rather than the conclusion itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based training and reports training classification error, but the benchmark tasks are binarized, use the paper's CNN/FC architectures and SGD recipe, and stop when training accuracy reaches 100%.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Boolean-function task, plain SGD often failed to reach zero training error, while advSGD succeeded in almost all cases; Adam learned the Boolean functions only with mean-squared error, according to Appendix A.

fits_no_version.finding: Plain SGD often failed to fit Boolean-function training sets perfectly after many thousand iterations, whereas advSGD succeeded in almost all cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization success in the tested small fully connected Boolean-function network depends on the training algorithm.

fits_no_version.finding: The fully connected benchmark network and the CNN on binarized MNIST and fashion-MNIST also attained zero training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can interpolate corrupted binary image datasets beyond convolutional CIFAR classifiers.

record.problems: Benchmark training-error results are stated only as an aggregate across experiments, without per-dataset or per-corruption values. The Boolean-task success statements are qualitative and lack exact rates.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing rows left out. The paper's cited results from prior studies are not rows.

untested.parts: Original multiclass CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Adam training on those datasets, model-size comparisons, and substantial training error under early stopping or regularized recipes. Stopping upon reaching 100% accuracy does not test stopping before interpolation.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and prevention through residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth. Varying Gaussian-process prior variances measures bounds and sampling agreement, not these training effects.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No limits_scope verdict follows from the Boolean-task failures because those rows fall outside the stated versions. The study is not an original source for V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests binarized MNIST, fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 with label corruption and Boolean-function learning. It does not test CIFAR-100, random labels on the original multiclass CIFAR task, Adam on the benchmark experiments, or comparisons of benchmark model sizes and early stopping.

rows.note: The reported aggregate covers the experiments across both architectures, all three datasets and the tested label-corruption levels. The text does not give separate training-error values by condition.
rows.check: Split this aggregate by architecture and dataset: only the CNN on binarized CIFAR-10 directly bears on V1. The fully connected network and MNIST/fashion-MNIST conditions should have versions ["none"]. Figure 3 reports zero training error across its experiments and averages generalization errors over eight initializations. Its zero-error statement should not be extended to every experiment elsewhere in the paper.

rows.check: The qualitative SGD failure result is accurately extracted, but a fully connected Boolean-function network does not test V1's convolutional CIFAR setting. It also does not test V2: there is no two-layer teacher-student width comparison or identification of spurious local minima.
